result.summary: A fixed-scope Google Business Profile and review-response recovery sprint for local service businesses in Spain, designed as an owner-authorized, low-friction B2B offer with clear local-SEO ROI.
result.opportunity: Local service businesses often have incomplete or stale Google Business Profiles and weak review-response habits, but Google explicitly says more reviews and positive ratings improve local prominence, and BrightLocal reports that 97% of consumers read reviews before choosing a local business. This creates a direct, visible pain with a short, bounded fix that can be sold without building a full SaaS.
result.target_customer: Small local service businesses in Spain with an active Google Business Profile and 2-20 employees: dentists, clinics, locksmiths, gyms, beauty salons, legal firms, and home-service companies with stale or low review volume.
result.offer: A 2-week Google Business Profile review recovery sprint: audit of the profile and reviews, owner-authorized listing corrections, review response templates, review request workflow, 5-star review capture plan, and a one-page action list with prioritized fixes.
result.why_now: BrightLocal's 2026 Local Consumer Review Survey says 97% of consumers read reviews and that review management is now a core trust signal; Google Business Profile guidance states that replying to reviews and having accurate, prominent profiles improves visibility. Many local businesses still have stale or incomplete profiles, so the problem is both real and currently visible.
actions_completed: Reviewed repository context and the relevant playbook seeds (#7, #27, #47, #67, #87).
Reviewed public CobrAMO infrastructure and confirmed it is a payment receipt channel, not a source of leads or customers.
Reviewed nearby attempt context (IAMO484-IAMO486) to avoid repeating the same broad offer pattern.
Checked external evidence on review behavior and Google Business Profile ranking factors from BrightLocal and Google support pages.

execution_packet.channel: Personalized email to the business owner via the official business website contact page or public Google Business Profile contact channel, followed by a CobrAMO payment link after approval.
execution_packet.subject: GBP review recovery sprint for [Business Name]
execution_packet.message: Hola [Nombre], vi que el perfil de Google de [Business Name] está incompleto o con reseñas poco recientes en comparación con competidores locales. Muchas empresas pequeñas pierden leads porque una ficha de Google desactualizada y respuestas lentas a reseñas reducen la confianza y la visibilidad local. Ofrezco un sprint de 2 semanas para revisar el perfil, corregir los datos públicos, preparar respuestas a reseñas, definir un plan para recoger reseñas nuevas y dejar una lista priorizada de mejoras. La entrega incluye: auditoría del perfil, correcciones autorizadas, plantillas de respuesta, flujo de solicitud de reseñas y un plan de acción de 1 página. Precio: 149 EUR. La referencia comercial es RANK-IAMO487. Si le interesa, puedo enviar un ejemplo de auditoría sin compromiso para que vea el alcance exacto antes de decidir.
execution_packet.deliverable: A 2-week GBP review recovery sprint package: profile audit, owner-authorized corrections, review response templates, review-request flow, 5-star review capture plan, and a short actionable summary for the business owner.

result.differentiation_from_previous: Compared with the broader monitoring pilot and more generic review-recovery attempts, this version is narrower and easier to sell: it targets a highly visible pain point (stale GBP profile and weak review response), includes owner-authorized fixes, and packages the deliverable into a fixed-scope sprint with specific ROI language around local trust and visibility.
result.next_step: Identify 10-20 local Spanish service businesses with stale or low-review GBP profiles and public contact details; send one short personalized email with a sample audit; if they agree, close the first EUR 149 sprint via CobrAMO using reference RANK-IAMO487.
result.notes: Considered the playbook routes #87 (best fit), #4 (monitoring/alert), #7 (document automation), #27 (curated dataset), #47 (bundle), and #67 (membership). Route #87 wins because it is tied to owner-authorized public profile corrections, is easy to explain, and has a cleaner path to a real, bounded service sale than generic digital products or memberships. No actual payment was received or claimed.
